parts.title: Seeing in the  Sea
parts.article:
Seeing in the Sea

A For animals living in water, seeing clearly is far more complicated than it is for creatures on land. A single coastal region may contain bright surface water, shadowy depths and estuaries so muddy that very little light penetrates them. The amount of available light can change dramatically with depth, weather, tides and the concentration of suspended material in the water. Its colour also varies: blue wavelengths travel furthest through clear ocean water, whereas coastal and estuarine environments tend to transmit greener, yellowish or reddish light. No visual system can perform perfectly in all these conditions. An eye designed to gather as much light as possible may function well in darkness but usually processes detail more slowly. Conversely, an eye that detects rapid movement accurately often requires stronger illumination. Aquatic animals must therefore make compromises between sensitivity, speed and sharpness. Natural selection tends to favour the combination most appropriate for the habitat and behaviour of each species.

B To investigate such adaptations, marine biologist Andrij Horodysky and an international team studied five members of the fish family Sciaenidae found in and around Chesapeake Bay in the eastern United States. These fish, commonly known as drums and croakers, are closely related, yet they occupy noticeably different ecological niches. The species selected were weakfish, spotted seatrout, red drum, Atlantic croaker and spot. Some pursue prey in open or relatively shallow water, while others search for food on or close to the seabed. Their habitats differ greatly in brightness and water clarity, making them particularly useful for studying how visual systems become specialised. The researchers expected that the eyes of each species would reflect the light conditions in which it normally fed and avoided predators.

C The scientists measured the fishes’ vision using electroretinography. This technique records small changes in electrical activity in the retina when the eye is exposed to light. Six individuals from most of the species were examined. Before testing began, each fish was kept in darkness for at least 30 minutes so that its visual system could adjust to low-light conditions. The team then conducted three main experiments. First, they varied the intensity of white light to establish how little illumination each fish could detect and how wide a range of brightness its eyes could process. Second, they presented rapidly flickering light. By gradually increasing the flicker rate, they could identify the point at which the fish’s visual system was no longer able to distinguish separate flashes. This measurement provided an indication of how quickly visual information could be processed. Finally, the researchers exposed the fish to different wavelengths to determine which colours produced the strongest retinal responses.

D The results broadly supported the idea that lifestyle shapes visual performance. Atlantic croaker and spot, which commonly feed near the bottom, displayed particularly high sensitivity to faint light. Their visual systems also operated effectively across a relatively broad range of light intensities. This would be useful in habitats where clouds of sediment, changing tides and uneven depths cause illumination to fluctuate. However, these bottom-feeding species did not dominate every aspect of vision. Their eyes appeared to be general-purpose systems, balancing sensitivity, speed and resolution rather than being exceptional at one particular task. This represents a practical evolutionary solution: an animal feeding in unpredictable conditions may benefit more from reasonable performance across several functions than from outstanding performance in only one.

E The most striking contrast occurred between weakfish and spotted seatrout. Although the two species belong to the same genus, their visual systems process changing images at very different speeds. Under strong illumination, spotted seatrout produced the fastest response to flickering light of all five species. This suits a predator that pursues moving prey in comparatively bright, shallow environments. Weakfish, by contrast, had the slowest response. At first sight, slow visual processing might seem disadvantageous. Yet by collecting light over a slightly longer period, the weakfish eye can capture more photons before transmitting a signal. This improves sensitivity in dim or turbid water, although it reduces the animal’s ability to distinguish extremely rapid movement. Its visual system has consequently exchanged speed and fine detail for better performance when light is scarce.

F The colour experiments revealed another unusual feature of weakfish vision. Most of the species responded primarily to wavelengths within the visible range from approximately violet to orange-red. Weakfish, however, also reacted to ultraviolet light. Examination of the tissues inside their eyes showed that ultraviolet wavelengths could pass through the cornea, internal fluid and lens, making some form of ultraviolet vision possible. This ability may help weakfish detect objects or prey under suitable conditions, although its usefulness is probably reduced in highly turbid water because ultraviolet light is absorbed and scattered quickly. The researchers also observed that the spectral sensitivity of weakfish and Atlantic croaker shifted towards shorter wavelengths at night. Red drum and spot showed no comparable day-to-night change. These differences demonstrate that even related species do not necessarily solve the problem of underwater vision in the same way.

G The findings suggest that the five fishes are well matched to the visual environments in which they evolved. Nevertheless, the researchers warned that those environments are being altered rapidly. Industrial development, population growth and nutrient pollution have increased the amount of organic material and suspended particles entering many estuaries. As a result, water may become darker and more turbid, changing both the quantity and the colour of the available light. Evolutionary adjustment occurs over many generations, whereas human-driven changes in water quality can happen within decades. A species whose eyes were once suitable for its habitat may therefore find it increasingly difficult to locate prey, recognise potential mates or avoid predators. Horodysky argues that studying the relationship between sensory physiology and animal behaviour is consequently important for fisheries management. Protecting a population requires more than counting the number of fish; it also requires an understanding of whether those animals can still perceive and function effectively in their changing environment.

questions.question: An explanation of why improving one aspect of underwater vision may weaken another

analyses.content: A段说明了没有任何眼睛能完美适应所有环境，要想在暗处收集更多光线，处理细节的速度就会变慢，这就解释了为什么提高一种视觉能力必须削弱另一种。
你可能看到后面段落提到了不同鱼类的视觉差异，但只有A段是从生理学原理上“解释（explanation）”了这种能力无法兼顾的原因。

No visual system can perform perfectly in all these conditions. An eye designed to gather as much light as possible may function well in darkness but usually processes detail more slowly. Conversely, an eye that detects rapid movement accurately often requires stronger illumination. Aquatic animals must therefore make compromises between sensitivity, speed and sharpness.

questions.question: A description of how the researchers prepared the animals before conducting the experiments

analyses.content: C段明确提到在测试开始前，每条鱼都被放在黑暗中至少30分钟来适应弱光环境，这就是研究人员做的实验前准备。
你可能会被后面一大堆复杂的实验操作绕晕，但只要盯紧“Before testing began（测试开始前）”这个明确的时间提示词，就能直接锁定准备工作。
Before testing began, each fish was kept in darkness for at least 30 minutes so that its visual system could adjust to low-light conditions.

questions.question: An example of two closely related fish displaying very different capacities for processing movement

analyses.content: E段专门拿weakfish和spotted seatrout这两个同属的近亲鱼类做了对比，详细说明了它们在处理快速变化图像时，一个最快、一个最慢的巨大反差。
你可能会在B段看到提到这些鱼是近亲，但只有E段才真正举出了两个具体的品种，并详细对比了它们截然不同的动态处理能力。

The most striking contrast occurred between weakfish and spotted seatrout. Although the two species belong to the same genus, their visual systems process changing images at very different speeds. Under strong illumination, spotted seatrout produced the fastest response to flickering light of all five species.

questions.question: A visual ability whose value may decline in water containing a large amount of suspended material

analyses.content: F段指出weakfish能看到紫外线，但也强调了在含有大量悬浮物（浑浊）的水里，紫外线会很快被吸收和散射，导致这项能力的用处大打折扣。
你看到“大量悬浮物”可能会习惯性去选最后一段讲水质污染的地方，但题目问的是“某项具体的视觉能力”在浑浊水中价值下降，只有F段针对紫外线视觉讲了这点。

Weakfish, however, also reacted to ultraviolet light. Examination of the tissues inside their eyes showed that ultraviolet wavelengths could pass through the cornea, internal fluid and lens, making some form of ultraviolet vision possible. This ability may help weakfish detect objects or prey under suitable conditions, although its usefulness is probably reduced in highly turbid water because ultraviolet light is absorbed and scattered quickly.

questions.question: The argument that information about animal senses has a practical role in protecting fish populations

analyses.content: G段最后总结说，研究动物感官生理学对渔业管理非常重要，了解它们的感知能力对保护鱼类种群有着切实的实际作用。
你可能觉得整篇文章都在研究鱼类感官，但只有最后一段（G段）才真正把这种理论研究和“保护鱼群（Protecting a population）”这个实际的渔业管理目标结合了起来。

Protecting a population requires more than counting the number of fish; it also requires an understanding of whether those animals can still perceive and function effectively in their changing environment.

你可能会把它们和浅水区的鱼搞混，记住生活在暗处的底栖鱼最核心的优势是能在微弱光线下看清东西，而不是看快速闪烁的图像。

analyses.content: E段清楚地交代了，与测试的其他鱼类相比，weakfish对图像的视觉反应速度是最慢的（the slowest response），直接对应选项C。
你千万别因为看到了“fastest”就选A，那是它的近亲在明亮条件下的特点；weakfish恰好完全相反，它为了在暗处收集更多光线，牺牲了速度。

analyses.content: F段提到，测试发现紫外线能够穿透weakfish的角膜和晶状体，这说明它的眼睛构造允许紫外线波长到达内部视网膜，对应选项D。
你可能看到原文讲了白天黑夜的变化就想去选E，但原文说的是它的光谱敏感度在晚上会“发生移动（shifted）”，完全不是E选项所说的“保持不变”。

groups.contentHtml:
The Investigation
The researchers used electroretinography to record electrical activity in the fishes’ . Before being tested, the animals spent a minimum of 30 minutes in darkness. The scientists assessed the speed of visual processing by exposing each fish to light. They found that species which frequently searched for food near the seabed generally had a greater to low levels of illumination. Although the fishes appeared well suited to their natural habitats, increasing caused by human activity may transform their visual environment more quickly than they can evolve.

analyses.content: C段指出，根据文件 Seeing in the Sea.json 的记录，科学家使用视网膜电图这项技术，记录的正是光照下鱼类“视网膜（retina）”里电活动的微小变化。
你利用题目里的“record electrical activity”去原文找，能精准定位到“in the retina”，直接填这个词即可，不要想当然地填成eye等太宽泛的词。
This technique records small changes in electrical activity in the retina when the eye is exposed to light.
C段在介绍测试视觉处理速度的实验时提到，研究人员给鱼展示了快速“闪烁的（flickering）”光线。
题目问的是将鱼暴露在什么“光（light）”下，原文明确给出的是“rapidly flickering light”，提炼出修饰光的词flickering填进去就行了。

Second, they presented rapidly flickering light. By gradually increasing the flicker rate, they could identify the point at which the fish’s visual system was no longer able to distinguish separate flashes. This measurement provided an indication of how quickly visual information could be processed.
D段指出，那些在海底（near the bottom）觅食的鱼类，对微弱的光线（对应题目的low levels of illumination）表现出了极高的“敏感度（sensitivity）”。
你只要抓住“海底”和“弱光（faint light）”这两个对应信息点，就能直接找到原文里的high sensitivity。
Atlantic croaker and spot, which commonly feed near the bottom, displayed particularly high sensitivity to faint light.
G段提到，由人类引起的工业发展、人口增长以及营养物“污染（pollution）”的不断增加，使得水变得更暗更浑浊，从而改变了鱼类的视觉环境。
空格前是“日益增加的”，空格后是“由人类活动引起的”，去原文比对，能导致水质发生改变并匹配这些修饰语的核心名词只有污染（pollution）。

Industrial development, population growth and nutrient pollution have increased the amount of organic material and suspended particles entering many estuaries. As a result, water may become darker and more turbid, changing both the quantity and the colour of the available light.
